messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert - spike of TLS handshake failures for inference edge in ap-south-1. 94 alerts in 6m. Source: LB healthcheck and frontend logs.
alex: ack - I'm oncall. paging infra + network. @clara @nate please join.
pagerduty: page sent to alex (primary). escalation clara next.
clara: seeing ~1.8% error uplift; several enterprise tenants reporting timeouts and 502s. starting triage.
support-bot: sent holding message to affected tenants; status page updated to "investigating".
infra: grabbed a few frontend logs:
```
2026-05-11T14:07:22Z frontend-12 tls: handshake failure: alert handshake_failure
2026-05-11T14:07:24Z frontend-15 tls: handshake failure: record overflow
2026-05-11T14:07:25Z frontend-12 conn: reset by peer during handshake
```
alex: mixed errors across nodes. can someone run an in-vpc client test and tcpdump? want to see MSS/DF and any ICMP messages.
nate: running openssl s_client and a curl from control-plane jump:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect edge-ap-south.redwood-internal:443 -tls1_2 -msg
... ClientHello
*** Alert: fatal, description = handshake failure
$ curl -v --http1.1 https://edge-ap-south.redwood-internal
* SSL: handshake failure
```
clara: infra, any recent network changes in region?
infra: we ran an MTU pilot earlier today: bumped ENI MTU -> 9000 in ap-south-1 at 13:45 UTC to test jumbo frames for throughput. Also there was a scheduled cert-rotation job starting at 14:00 UTC.
alex: two concurrent risky changes. hypothesis: PMTU blackhole from jumbo frames + concurrent cert rotation increases ClientHello size -> handshake fails for some flows. but let's prove it.
infra: pulled cert serials from nodes:
- frontend-11: serial 0xAAA111 (issued 2026-05-01)
- frontend-12: serial 0xBBB222 (issued 2026-05-11)
- frontend-13: serial 0xBBB222 (issued 2026-05-11)
note: partial rotation in progress.
nate: tcpdump snippet on frontend-12 (failing):
```
14:06:58.100 IP 10.50.60.7.50123 > 34.77.88.10.443: Flags [S], seq 201, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
14:06:58.205 IP 34.77.88.10.443 > 10.50.60.7.50123: Flags [S.], seq 400, ack 202, options [mss 1400], length 0
14:06:58.208 IP 10.50.60.7.50123 > 34.77.88.10.443: Flags [P.], seq 202:472, ack 401, length 270
14:06:58.208 IP 34.77.88.10.443 > 10.50.60.7.50123: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, length 0
```
alex: server MSS 1400, client 1460, server resets after ClientHello. pattern matches PMTU-related drops.
clara: ran DF ping from jumpbox: `ping -M do -s 1420 34.77.88.10` -> no reply. `-s 1200` -> reply. Also not seeing ICMP type3(code4) in captures.
network: we pushed a transit-route ACL change yesterday that default-denies ICMP across peered VPCs. That could silence PMTU ICMP messages.
infra: so chain: ENI MTU -> jumbo frames produced larger ClientHello -> path includes an interface that cannot handle jumbo, drops DF packets -> no fragmentation-needed ICMP returns because ACL drops ICMP -> client doesn't know to reduce size -> server sees incomplete/bad TLS record -> RST/handshake_failure.
alex: immediate mitigations - propose in-order: (1) rollback ENI MTU to 1500 region-wide, (2) pause cert-rotation to prevent adding variability, (3) open provider ticket about peering and PMTU, (4) temporarily allow ICMP frag-needed between critical subnets. Agree?
clara: agree. infra canary rollback in ap-south-1a first.
infra: starting canary rollback in 1a now. watch healthchecks and handshake-fail metric.
(--- 4m)
infra: canary result: nodes in 1a show handshake failures drop from 30/min to 0-1/min. healthchecks green.
clara: rolling back remaining AZs. pause cert-rotation.
(--- 7m)
infra: full rollback complete. aggregated TLS handshake failure metric back to baseline within 3-5m.
support-bot: updated customers: partial resolution; services returning to normal for most tenants. We're monitoring for 60m.
alex: handing oncall to clara for RCA follow-up. I'm logging the incident timeline.
clara: starting quick timeline and evidences in-thread:
Timeline (approx):
- 13:45 UTC: ENI MTU change to 9000 in ap-south-1 (pilot)
- 14:00 UTC: cert-rotation job kicked off for edge LBs (staged)
- 14:06 UTC: first TLS handshake_failure alerts
- 14:07 UTC: incident created and paging initiated
- 14:12 UTC: canary MTU rollback started (1a)
- 14:19 UTC: region-wide MTU rollback complete
- 14:24 UTC: TLS errors back to baseline; monitoring
Evidence uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/2125551234/evidence/ (pcaps, cert-lists, lb-logs)
Initial hypotheses (blameless):
1) Primary: PMTU blackhole caused by enabling jumbo ENI MTU combined with transit path that does not support jumbo and blocks ICMP frag-needed. Evidence: tcpdump MSS mismatch, DF-ping failures, no ICMP observed, rollback cured.
2) Contributing: Partial cert rotation changed ClientHello size/extension set making some CHs exceed MTU more often. Evidence: mixed cert serials across nodes and rotation overlap.
3) Tertiary: TLS offload/bufferization differences on LB instances can affect packetization sizes. Evidence: different node error messages.
Follow-ups / Action items (owner):
- infra: create MTU change playbook with mandatory PMTU preflight and canary window; require provable DF-ping checks before region rollouts. (@infra)
- network: update transit-gw/peering ACLs to allow ICMP type3 code4 between peered VPCs and document expected PMTU behavior in runbook. (@network)
- platform: change cert-rotation to check handshake success on canary nodes and delay further rollout on any handshake anomalies; include MTU awareness in rollout gating. (@platform)
- observability: add alerting for rapid spikes in tls handshake_failure ratio and a synthetic PMTU probe that runs when MTU changes occur. (@obs)
- cloud-ops: open ticket with provider to verify physical path MTU and any encapsulation (VXLAN/GRE) that impacts fragment sizes. (@cloud-ops)
- support: prepare customer-facing RCA draft and hold until RCA review. (@support)
sre-lead: please ensure action owners and SLAs for tasks. We'll schedule postmortem in 48h and follow blameless practice.
deploy-bot: cert-rotation job paused for ap-south-1 until manual resume.
clara: I'll own the RCA doc. uploading artifacts and will send draft to #postmortems + customer comms for review. handoff: @clara will be oncall for post-incident until 17:00 UTC.
alex: thanks team. good mitigation. closing incident as mitigated -> monitoring. next update in 45m or earlier if regression.
(--- thread end)
